references.text: John 8:17 directly quoted the law that two witnesses are necessary to establish a case, as set forth in Deuteronomy 19:15.
The principle that a case cannot be decided on the basis of one witness but requires two or three is repeated in Deuteronomy 17:6.
Paul reminds the Corinthians that every case must stand firm on the testimony of two or three witnesses, in accordance with the law's requirement.
Hebrews draws a contrast between the death penalty for breaking the law with two witnesses and the even harsher punishment for despising God's Son, who has more witnesses.
